why.headline: Springy ankles help you jump high and push off fast.

claims.text: In studies with adult players, keepers jumped higher than outfield players.
Saves need a fast first push. In a youth trial, hop and bound drills made short sprints quicker.
Early-teen players swapped some football drills for jumps twice a week. After 8 weeks, jump tests were 7.9 to 10.9% higher.
Younger boys added hops, skips and shuffles twice a week. After 12 weeks, jump tests were 16 to 23% higher.

keep_up.text: Keep training it every week to keep gains coming. In one youth study, jump gains lasted 8 weeks after training stopped. Everyone improves at their own pace.

map.plain: Your calf muscles, at the back of your lower legs
The muscle down the front of your shin

note.text: Hopping studies measured these muscles in adults; none measured them in teens.

claims.text: In adults, quicker hops switched the calves on before landing. That made the legs springier.
In a 4-week youth trial, hop training made older groups' legs springier. The youngest group did not change.

limits.text: No study has tested pogo hops alone in goalkeepers. The youth trials used many kinds of jumps.
